title: Estimating by analogy, parametrically and by three points

videos.script: Ask four people how long their task will take, and add up the answers. {{ask}} For the Agenda team, that gives seventeen days. It is the number most plans are built from. {{seventeen}} It is also the most optimistic number on the table. Each answer was the most likely value, and a task can run much longer than expected, but only a little shorter. {{tail}} This lesson estimates the same feature three ways. By analogy, from a feature the team already built. By a rate, from screens it already made. And by three points per task, optimistic, most likely and pessimistic. {{three}} The three methods agree within two days. That agreement is the strongest evidence an estimate can have. {{agree}} Then you add the tasks up properly, and learn to say a range with a confidence instead of one number that will be heard as a promise. {{range}}
